transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to see me?

Um, hi. I guess... I'm just having a lot of trouble focusing on things. Like, I'll be trying to fill out a job application or something, and... I don't know, a car drives by outside, or my phone lights up, and I just get completely derailed. Or even just a random thought pops into my head and I'm off doing something else before I even realize I stopped what I was supposed to be doing. It's just... hard to stay on track.
How long have you been experiencing these trouble focusing and getting distracted? Has this been going on since childhood, or is this something more recent?

Um... not since childhood, no. It's more recent. I guess... it got this disruptive about a year and ten months ago. I had a soccer injury, and... it just kind of knocked me out of my usual routine. It's been worse since then.
Over this past year and ten months, have you been feeling persistently sad, down, or empty most days?
Um... no. Not really. I mean, I don't think so. I don't really feel sad or anything... just normal, I guess.
When you're trying to focus on something, do you notice that you're feeling worried or anxious about things, or does your mind just wander without any sense of worry?
Um... I don't really feel worried. My mind just... wanders, I guess. I'm not anxious about it, just... distracted.
When you had that soccer injury about a year and ten months ago, did you hit your head or lose consciousness at all?
Um... no. No, it was just my knee. I didn't hit my head or anything like that.
After your knee injury, did you have any other symptoms like headaches, dizziness, memory problems, or just not feeling like yourself physically — anything besides the knee pain that's stuck around?
No... I don't think so. It was really just my knee. I didn't have headaches or anything like that.
Besides trying to fill out job applications, do you notice these attention problems happening in other areas of your life too — like at work, at home, or in social situations?

Yeah... I guess so. Like with my training. I've missed some deadlines for it... and I keep having to redo applications. So I'm just kind of stuck. I want to be an auto tech, and I know I can do the hands-on work fine... I'm just not really moving forward with it.
Before you had that soccer injury about a year and ten months ago, were you able to focus and concentrate on things pretty well, or were you already having trouble with attention back then?

Um... no, it's not new. It's been like this for a long time. Even back in elementary school... I remember teachers were always moving my desk. They said I talked out of turn too much. And I'd forget my homework... or just rush through the worksheets and make stupid mistakes. So... yeah, it's been a while.

latest_inference.note: Ruled out F98.8. The soccer injury 22 months ago appears to be coincidental timing rather than causative of a new condition.
